agree.reason: The plain account of the late report, with a named owner and quarterly updates, would reassure Marisol. She would still hold off on a yes until she knows who pays to run the van once the purchase drains reserves to $11,000.

honest.reason: The draft rightly drops the unsupported 'double' claim and every figure is accurate. But it leaves out the $4,500 a year in insurance and fuel that isn't budgeted, and it rounds 62% of reserves up to 'nearly two-thirds'.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out several correct figures: under 10 lb of fresh food per household each month, summer fresh food rising from 18,000 to 27,000 lb (up by half), and nearly 15 extra lb per household. Each one is framed in its strongest true form.

right_comparison.reason: The no-van case is described honestly as the same fresh food going out while farm offers are turned down again. It doesn't say whether the van would be used outside the summer season.

qualification.reason: The report deadline and quarterly totals are dated and can be checked. The hedge on farm supply sets no target in pounds and says nothing about what happens if the van brings in less than expected.

objections.reason: It meets the late-report objection head-on. It leaves open the obvious question of how a $4,500-a-year operating cost gets paid from $11,000 in reserves.

fit.reason: It is a narrative section of roughly 450 words, inside the 500-word limit and in the right register for a grant application.
